ksr_caveat_closure_analysis.method: Re-fetched patent page with full description extraction (99,514 chars). Separate OX Alpha call asked 5 specific questions about description-level teaching of elements (a), (b), (c) and KSR combination plausibility.
ksr_caveat_closure_analysis.question_1_does_description_teach_elemen: NO. Description is exclusively about angiographic parametric imaging (API) of the vasculature via contrast time-density curves. No passage describes a sensor integrated with a retrieval device, no measurement of retrieved thrombus material's physical properties (composition, stiffness, impedance, optical/electrical signature), and no contact or ex-vivo sensing of retrieved material. The closest teaching is hemodynamic parameters derived from contrast flow — an indirect, remote, imaging-derived quantity, categorically different from direct physical sensing of retrieved thrombus.
ksr_caveat_closure_analysis.question_2_does_description_teach_elemen: NO for the combination as claimed. Description does teach intra-procedural outcome prediction generally (e.g., 'predict whether the intervention performed was successful or not based on the API data measured pre- and post treatment'), but inputs are API maps only; no teaching of pass count, device trajectory, or retrieved-clot physical properties as score inputs. sICH specifically is not mentioned.
ksr_caveat_closure_analysis.question_3_does_description_teach_elemen: PARTIALLY, at a generic level. Description states 'a surgeon may better determine whether additional intervention is appropriate' — a teaching that intra-procedural prediction can inform further intervention decisions. However, it is tied to API-based score, not retrieved-clot-signature-based score, and no specific gating logic (additional passes vs. adjunct therapy) is described.
ksr_caveat_closure_analysis.question_4_ksr_combination_assessment: Strongest combination attempt: WO2021108783A1 (intra-procedural outcome prediction + escalation motivation) + US11955237B2 (calibrated risk scoring) + US10531883B1 (thrombectomy apparatus). WHY IT FAILS: none of these references teaches or suggests measuring a physical signature of retrieved thrombus material by a retrieval-system-integrated sensor. WO2021108783A1's entire predictive pipeline is built on contrast-based API maps; substituting a direct clot-sensing modality would require importing a third reference that itself teaches element (a). The keystone input variable (retrieved-clot physical signature) appears in no cited reference.
ksr_caveat_closure_analysis.question_5_final_ksr_verdict: NO — caveat closed. WO2021108783A1's description does not teach element (a) even at description level. Its teachings are confined to angiographic/contrast-derived hemodynamic parameters of the vasculature. The candidate's element (a) — intra-procedural retrieved-clot physical signature measurement by a sensor integrated with the retrieval system — remains untaught by this reference. The Round 60 caveat regarding its description-level 'predicting outcome at the time of treatment' language resolves against obviousness support: that language supports only imaging-input scoring, which overlaps with (b)/(c) but not (a).
ksr_caveat_closure_analysis.residual_caveat: Analysis based on truncated description extract. If the full specification contains an embodiment of retrieval-device-integrated sensing (no indication of this in field, summary, or figure list — all figures concern API maps, CNNs, and aneurysm/stroke imaging), this verdict would need revision. Recommend a targeted full-text keyword sweep (sensor, thrombus composition, retrieved clot, histology) before final closure.
